notes.body: A card cannot test sound. Vowels and Read aloud are prompts for you to listen to and judge — the child has to say the vowel, not recognise it. Sound rules works on its own.

cards.f: What must never happen to an Italian vowel?
cards.m: It must never slide or be swallowed. The mouth stays still, and the final vowel is as strong as the first.

cards.f: Which letters in an Italian word are silent?
cards.m: Only h. Everything else is pronounced, including every final vowel.

notes.lead: The one deck they can do alone
notes.body: Hard or soft? needs no sound and marks itself, so it is the only deck in this unit a child can work through without you sitting there. Leave them to it.

cards.f: When is c hard, and when is it soft?
cards.m: Hard before a, o, u â casa, cosa, cura. Soft, like ch in chair, before e and i â cena, cinema.

cards.f: When is g hard, and when is it soft?
cards.m: Hard before a, o, u â gatto, gonna, gusto. Soft, like j in jam, before e and i â gelato, giro.

cards.f: What does an h do after c or g?
cards.m: Forces the hard sound back: chi, che, spaghetti, ghiaccio. The h itself is never pronounced.

cards.f: What does an i do after c or g, before a, o or u?
cards.m: Forces the soft sound: ciao, giornale. That i is not pronounced as a separate sound.

notes.body: A printed nonno / nono proves nothing. Minimal pairs and Read aloud only work if they say the word and you judge it. Use the pairs deck as the prompt list for the guessing game, not as a test.

cards.m: Like ny in canyon. One sound, not two. gnocchi, signore, bagno, lasagne.
Like lli in million, but softer and further back. famiglia, figlio, meglio, aglio.
Sh before e and i â pesce, sciare. Sk before a, o, u â scuola, scarpa. Same rule as c and g.

cards.f: What does a double consonant do in Italian?
cards.m: It is genuinely held longer, and it changes meaning: nonno and nono are different words.

notes.lead: How to use the Stress deck
notes.body: Have them say the word before turning the card over, then check. Guessing first is the whole exercise — the default is reliable enough that they should be right most of the time, and being right is what makes the rule stick.

cards.f: Where does the stress normally fall?
cards.m: On the second-to-last syllable: ca-SA, a-MI-co, spa-GHET-ti. The default is reliable.

cards.f: What does a written accent tell you â cittÃ , caffÃ¨, perchÃ©?
cards.m: That the stress falls on the final syllable. It is marked so you always know.
